subject: Regional SKU blackout, uplift escrow & distributor handling for Private Offer
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@clearmap.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@clearmap.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer question — EU SKU blackout impact on list price

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're finalizing the PO: the SKU mapping in the EU region shows a temporary blackout for the 'Reserved-HighMem' SKU next quarter. That SKU was the anchor for our committed nodehours. If we have to swap to the on-demand SKU mix (higher per-token cost) for that window, how will you reflect that in the private offer pricing?

Specifically: 1) Will the private offer netback assume the original SKU mix or will Redwood apply an uplift to handle the shortage? 2) If an uplift is applied, can that be ringfenced and paid through an escrow or passback to the distributor rather than changing the headline PO price?

We'd like to avoid a pricing rebook in our procurement review next week. Attaching a small workbook with our expected consumption pattern.

Thanks,
Alicia Torres
Head of Cloud Procurement
Clearmap

Attachment: pricing_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@clearmap.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer question — EU SKU blackout impact on list price

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear note and the workbook. Short answer: we can avoid changing the headline PO price if we use an uplift escrow and distributor passback for the short window. Longer answer below and a couple of asks.

Summary proposal:
- Keep PO list price and committed volumes as-is for the contract term.
- For the blackout window, create a temporary uplift bucket that covers the incremental per-token cost when we must serve on-demand SKUs.
- Hold the uplift in escrow (billing-admin) and route to the distributor as a passback once actual usage is reconciled.

Questions / dependencies for legal & finance:
1) Jordan / Naomi: will Redwood's billing support a temporally-scoped escrow line item on a private offer that is not reflected in the list price but appears on invoices as 'Blackout uplift (escrow)'?
2) If not, alternative is a conditional credit that gets refunded after reconciliation — any preference from finance?

Operational notes: we need to confirm acceptable accrual windows and reconciliation cadence (monthly vs. quarterly). Alicia — can you confirm the blackout dates and the expected percentage of nodehours impacted? Your workbook helps but we need one more slice by week.

I'll loop Vanessa (partner ops) if we need distributor contract language.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: jordan.blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private offer question — escrow/passback approach for SKU shortage

Folks — quick internal note before I respond to Alicia.

Finance/Legal options (high level):
- Option A (preferred): Billing supports a non-list escrow line item. We invoice gross, accrue the uplift to escrow, and passback to distributor after reconciliation. Keeps customer-facing PO static. Requires a simple addendum to distributor agreement.
- Option B: Add a conditional surcharge to the PO that is netted via a promised credit once usage is reconciled. More straightforward on billing side but customer will see a changed headline.

Operational constraints:
- Escrow requires a defined cap and reconciliation window. Recommend cap = 120% of forecasted uplift and monthly reconciliation for the blackout months.
- Distributor routing: Vanessa, can you confirm whether our distributor agreements allow short-term passbacks tied to usage reconciliation, or do we need a one-off contract amendment?

Naomi, if billing cannot model an escrow line item in HubSpot/Stripe stack quickly, we'll propose Option B to the customer with explicit language that credits will be issued post-window. We should keep the credit workflow documented in the PO addendum.

I'll draft a short email to Alicia proposing Option A and flag Option B as fallback.

-jordan
Head of Deal Operations, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@clearmap.com>
Cc: jordan.blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer question — EU SKU blackout impact on list price

Hi Alicia — looping back with a concrete path forward. Appreciate the workbook — we used it to size a capped escrow.

What we propose:
1) Keep the PO headline and committed volumes unchanged.
2) Add a one-page addendum that creates a 'Blackout Uplift Escrow' for the dates 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-31. Cap the escrow at EUR 45,000 (120% of the uplift forecasted in your workbook).
3) Redwood will invoice actual usage as normal. Any uplift attributable to on-demand SKU substitution during the blackout period will be accrued to the escrow. Monthly reconciliation will run within 10 business days of month close.
4) After reconciliation, Redwood will remit any excess (or invoice shortfall) to the distributor per the passback instructions in the addendum. If there is residual customer liability (usage beyond the escrow cap), we will surface that as a one-time invoice line and notify you 14 days ahead.

Attachments: I attached a redlined addendum and a short implementation note for billing and partner ops. Please review — if this looks good, I can route to procurement and legal for signatures.

Next steps for us: Jordan and Naomi will confirm final billing labeling and the exact invoice line item text. Vanessa — can you confirm distributor language by EOD tomorrow?

Alicia — thanks again for raising this early. If you want, we can set a 20-minute call to walk procurement/legal through the addendum.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0132
